The move comes as the statutory power to seize land under the 1927 Act is limited because much of the sanctuary is not a notified forest. The Central Empowered Committee (CEC) informed about these practical constraints in a review of the mining crackdown.

articles.title: From Australia to Europe, countries move to curb children's social media access
articles.summary: Several countries, including Australia, Britain, France, and Greece, are introducing laws to restrict social media access for children under specific ages (15 or 16) starting between 2025 and 2027. These measures aim to protect minors from online risks, prompting new regulations on tech companies for child safety and age verification. The trend reflects growing global concerns about the impact of social media on young users.
articles.raw_summary: Australia banned social media for children under sixteen, effective December 2025. Britain plans a similar ban for under-sixteens by Spring 2027. France and Greece are also implementing bans for children under fifteen. Many countries are now establishing minimum age limits for social media use. Tech companies face new regulations regarding child protection and age verification.

articles.title: US lawmakers urge Donald Trump to act against EU tech rules, suggest trade probes
articles.summary: US lawmakers have written to former President Donald Trump urging him to take action against the European Union's Digital Markets Act, which targets major tech firms like Amazon, Apple, Google, and Meta. The lawmakers argue that European businesses have unrestricted access to the US market, suggesting trade investigations as a response. The European Commission emphasized the importance of a transatlantic digital dialogue for mutual benefit.

articles.title: PPI vs WPI: What is Producer Price Index and why will it replace Wholesale Price Index in India?
articles.summary: India is phasing out the Wholesale Price Index for a new Producer Price Index. This shift aims to capture prices closer to the factory gate. Both indices will run in parallel for five years to allow business adjustments. Contracts currently referencing WPI will need recalibration during this transition. The government seeks to align with international practices and improve economic data.

articles.title: Kharif sowing gap narrows despite widening rainfall deficit; East, Central India may see improved rains: Report
articles.summary: India's Kharif sowing gap has narrowed despite a widening rainfall deficit, with rice acreage nearly matching last year's levels. Other crops like pulses and oilseeds also saw reduced shortfalls. Improved rainfall is forecast for East and Central India in the coming weeks, which could further aid agricultural recovery.

articles.title: Protein inflation surges as costlier fodder pushes up milk, chicken prices
articles.summary: Protein inflation in India rose to 4.6% in May, up from 2.6% in January, driven by higher costs of animal feed. Vegetarian protein sources also saw inflation increase to 3.5% in June. The rising costs of fodder have pushed up prices of milk and chicken, raising concerns about food affordability and potential policy responses to address agricultural input costs.
articles.raw_summary: Protein inflation was 4.6% in May and 2.6% in January, it showed. Inflation in vegetarian protein sources also gathered pace, rising to 3.5% in June from 2.7% in May, after remaining flat in January.

articles.title: Gratuity, leave encashment not part of CIRP cost: NCLAT
articles.summary: The National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) dismissed an appeal regarding the priority payment of gratuity dues for a former director of Duncans Industries. The tribunal upheld that gratuity and leave encashment are terminal benefits, not part of insolvency resolution costs, and must be settled under the company's approved resolution plan. The appeal was deemed misconceived and dismissed.
articles.raw_summary: The NCLAT dismissed an appeal regarding priority payment of gratuity dues. It upheld an earlier NCLT order concerning Duncans Industries' former director. Such dues must be settled according to the company's approved resolution plan. Gratuity is a terminal benefit, not an insolvency resolution process cost. The appellate tribunal found the appeal misconceived and dismissed it.
